title: introduce-utilization-slope-regulator-and-tailwind-autoscaler
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: Dedicated pools currently scale reactively to utilization windows which can miss short inflection points (sharp ramps) and lead to 200–500ms tail latencies as cold workers spin up. This PR introduces two coordinated features: a lightweight utilization-slope estimator (server-side) and a new autoscaler policy we call the Tailwind Autoscaler. The slope estimator produces a short-horizon derivative signal (utilization/sec and smoothed delta) that captures momentum in incoming load. Tailwind Autoscaler consumes the slope signal plus existing percentile windows to make preemptive, bounded reservations and warm-up hints for the warm pool.

What this changes (high level):
- runtime/autoscaler: add slope_regulator.go which computes an exponentially-weighted slope on per-pool and per-tenant utilization streams and exposes util_slope metrics.
- autoscaling policy: tailwind_policy.yaml — a new policy schema that configures horizon, momentum weight, max-prebook-percent, and warm-pool hints.
- controller: autoscaler now has a tailwind mode that uses slope to pre-reserve ephemeral capacity and issue warmlet allocations for low-latency fast-ramp paths.
- telemetry: util_slope_{p50,p95} metrics and a new util_slope_alerting rule in observability-pack.
- safety: an emergency-fuse that prevents prebooking if sustained downstream error rate or node saturation is detected to avoid cascading failures.

Operational notes and rollout: default disabled for stable tenants. Feature is gated by feature flag and by a new per-tenant opt-in in Dedicated configuration. Rollout plan: enable in Canary cluster for 72h with synthetic ramp tests, follow with staged enablement on low-risk tenants, then progressive rollout with a 2x-monitor window.

Benchmarks (canary results): with synthetic step-ramp tests we saw 9% reduction in P95 end-to-end request latency for bursty workloads and a 6% reduction in total cold-start CPU-time across the warm pool. Cost delta measured as marginal increase in short-lived reservations (~1.1% on synthetic) but net savings when accounting for SLA-driven retries.

Backward compatibility and safety: Tailwind policy is optional and off by default. No API breaking changes. The estimator runs as a separate goroutine with bounded memory and CPU; unit tests assert that pathological inputs do not produce negative reservations. The safety fuse ensures we never exceed per-pool budgeted headroom.

Notes on validation: included integration tests that run against the local autoscaler simulator (tests/autoscaler/tailwind_sim_test.go). Added end-to-end smoke scenario in perf-canary harness.

feat(policy): introduce tailwind autoscaler policy schema and default config
chore(telemetry): add util_slope metrics and observability rule
fix(safety): emergency fuse check for prebook path
test: unit + integration tests for slope estimator and tailwind behavior
docs: ops guide for tailwind-autoscaler and rollout playbook
review_threads: Daniel Kim (review): Nice design. A few requests: (1) add a short-circuit when pool utilisation < 5% to avoid noisy slopes, (2) document expected units on the slope metric. -- Maya replied: added fast-exit and clarified units in comments/metrics.

Sofia Martinez (comments): Safety fuse looks reasonable but can we gate prebook by recent node OOM events? -- Maya replied: added a resilience check to consult node-saturation summary and included a mocked check in integration tests.
Ethan Zhao (approval): Verified behavior in canary cluster, observed reduced p95 on burst tests. Approve after CI passes.
release_notes: Introduce Tailwind Autoscaler (opt-in). Adds utilization-slope telemetry, prebook reservations for short-horizon ramps, and an emergency fuse to bound risk. Default off for existing tenants.
